correctness.rationale: The Fourier ODE (d_y^2-rho^2)^2 f=0 has exactly the decaying 2-mode fiber (A+By)e^{-rho y}; direct Laguerre orthonormality and the integrated tail Gram matrix yield M=e^{-at}Q(at)-e^{-bt}Q(bt). Its determinant is e^{-cz}[2(cosh z-1)-z^2]. The analytic identity g'^2-gg''=2[z^2(cosh z+1)-4z sinh z+4(cosh z-1)] has a positive coefficient power series starting z^6/36 (independently symbolically verified), so g'/g decreases strictly from infinity to 1 and the c>1 optimum is unique. Small-z g~z^4/12 yields quartic thin-slab constant 64/(3e^4). The equation epsilon~z^2 e^{-z} yields z=L+2log L+o(1) and 1-D*~epsilon L. At a=0 the interval Gram increases toward I and the determinant supremum 1 is not attained. All claims concern fiber determinants, not a global Fredholm determinant.
